static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with friends and family, self-isolating out of guilt and shame
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; not yet received psychotherapy; no similar problem history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly well organized; able to describe events and emotions concretely; steady tone but Low mood; fairly cooperative; marked self-criticism

basic_info.main_problem: Experiences strong guilt and self-blame because the dog ran away from home, believing she is the 'worst pet owner in the world'.
basic_info.core_demands: The overwhelming Guilt and self-blame over my dog running away from home leave me overwhelmed, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: I am the worst pet owner

special_situations.event: When the dog ran out of the house, I was distracted looking at my phone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not stay attentive at all times to keep my pet safe, it means I am an irresponsible, failed owner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly blames themselves, recalls the details of the incident, and intensifies the search (posting posters, visiting neighbors, posting on social media)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I had not been looking at my phone, Max would not have run off; It is all my fault, I am the worst owner

special_situations.event: Every time thinking of the dog or seeing other pet owners interact with their pets
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep everything under control at all times like other owners, I do not deserve to have a pet
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Comparing with others, Avoids socializing to dodge shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not deserve a pet; I am just a terrible owner

special_situations.event: Each passing day the dog is still not found
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot find him quickly, it proves I keep failing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifies self-criticism; immersed in negative emotions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel worse and worse; this means I really am a complete failure

special_situations.event: Thinking that I am at Work and have not devoted all my time to searching for the dog
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must keep doing more nonstop, otherwise I am irresponsible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Berates himself with 'should/must' standards, sacrificing rest and social life
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do more; if I have not done more, I am an irresponsible owner

core_conflict.wish: Longs to guard and maintain a stable attachment relationship with the pet, and to be seen as a responsible caregiver worthy of being loved / trusted
core_conflict.fear: Fear of losing important relationships and self-worth through my own negligence, being seen by others or myself as incompetent
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control and morality over the event through Reinforcement self-blame
Avoiding shame and external evaluation by keeping distance and self-isolating

object_relations.object_representation: A pet let down by oneself, fragile and needing protection

object_relations.self_representation: Someone unworthy of interacting with others, a low-value individual
object_relations.object_representation: Groups of others/pet owners who are more responsible and will evaluate oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests contacting family/friends for support or discussing self-care
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client worries that speaking up will expose an 'incompetent' side, believing others will judge negatively (transference: projecting self-criticism onto others' perspective)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing in self-blaming language (e.g., 'It is all my fault'), lowering self-worth, refusing or postponing help-seeking, in a restrained tone, avoiding deeper support from others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes a concrete action plan and evaluates pros and cons
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client understands the outcome in black-and-white terms: not yet fully recovering the pet counts as total failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in absolutist, all-or-nothing terms (e.g., 'either find Max or I am the worst owner'), in a tense tone, ignoring middle possibilities.

manifestations: Self-isolates; avoids contact with friends and family
Finds it hard to express inner feelings to family and friends, afraid of exposing a 'failed' self
Bound by the Introjected value of 'should/must do more', experiencing responsibility pressure and harsh self-criticism
outcomes: Life rhythm out of balance, body-mind load increased

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judges whether she is competent by external ideal standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strong self-blame and self-criticism, believing I do not deserve to ask for help
Contacting others with excessive caution, worried about exposing a 'failure' image

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Could have sought support from friends and family but instead turns to self-blame and inner torment
Reduces outgoing expression and help-seeking under shame

positive_force: Deep affection and sense of responsibility for the pet
Still takes proactive action under high pressure (posting posters, visiting neighbors, contacting shelters)
Has a certain tendency toward realistic problem solving (willing to evaluate options and make plans)
Has potential support resources (several friends and one sister)
negative_force: Strong guilt and self-blame tendency (personalization, absolutization)
Self-isolation and avoiding help-seeking, Social withdrawal
Sleep and diet affected, low energy and Reduced work focus
Rigid 'should/must' standards leading to excessive self-harshness

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent rumination of self-blame and guilt
antecedent: Seeing other pet owners interact with their pets
Being distracted at work triggers associations with the event
target_behavior.core_reason: The event triggers strong responsibility attribution and personalization, with a black-and-white cognitive pattern ('It is all my fault' 'I am the worst owner')
target_behavior.function: Maintaining control and morality through self-criticism, avoiding external judgment and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, insomnia and reduced appetite, Interpersonal tension and self-isolation, Increased emotional burden

antecedent: Anticipation others may ask about or judge the incident
Discomfort at the thought of expressing inner feelings to family and friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being seen by others as incompetent, internalizing the high-standard 'should', causing shame and a sense of undeservingness
target_behavior.function: Avoiding shame and potential negative judgment, short-term Anxiety relief
target_behavior.consequence: Weakened support system, Interpersonal tension, emotional distress maintained or even worsened
